name: Margaret River

climate: Cabernet Sauvignon and Shiraz sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

keyfacts: Margaret River is in southwest Western Australia, with 215 wineries as of 2012.
Its climate is more strongly maritime than any other major Australian region, with a mean annual temperature range of only 13.7°F.
Rainfall is strongly Mediterranean, with little of it falling between October and April, and overall the climate resembles Bordeaux in a dry vintage.
The main grapes are Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Semillon, Shiraz, Merlot and Chenin Blanc.
There are no official subregions, but in 1999 John Gladstones suggested six: Yallingup, Carbunup, Wilyabrup, Treeton, Wallcliffe and Karridale.

blurb.text: A boutique-scale region in southwest Western Australia, in the South West Australia area, and the most maritime-influenced of the major Australian regions, with a Mediterranean pattern of rainfall. Cabernet Sauvignon is 26 percent of plantings, then Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz and Semillon.
